facts.text: I've lost some of the vision in both eyes.

facts.item: how long the vision problems have lasted
facts.text: It all started 3 years ago, a few days after I accidentally swallowed the niclosamide.

facts.item: how the vision problems have changed over time
facts.text: Over these 3 years my vision problems have stayed the same.

facts.item: accidental ingestion of a veterinary drug
facts.text: Three years ago I accidentally swallowed four 1250 mg boluses of a veterinary niclosamide product.
At that time the doctors thought I had optic neuritis in both eyes.
I was treated with a short course of high-dose steroid tablets for it.
My vision neither got better nor got worse with them.
I don't take any other medicines.
I don't have trouble seeing in the dark.

facts.item: vision loss or retinal disease in the family
facts.text: No one in my family has had vision loss or retinal disease.
My parents are not related to each other by blood.

findings.name: best-corrected visual acuity
findings.result: 20/50 in the right eye; 20/63 in the left eye.

findings.name: fundoscopy
findings.result: Pink optic discs, cup-to-disc ratios of 0.2; parafoveal retinal pigment epithelial atrophy manifesting as bilateral bull's-eye maculopathy.

findings.name: fundus autofluorescence
findings.result: Annular hyperautofluorescence in the parafoveal region.

findings.name: optical coherence tomography
findings.result: Parafoveal ellipsoid zone disruption, outer retinal thinning, and relative foveal sparing ("flying saucer" sign).

findings.name: full-field electroretinography
findings.result: Decreased scotopic and photopic amplitudes with normal waveforms in both eyes.

gold.reasoning: 1. Chloroquine toxicity was contemplated based on imaging patterns — “Significant thinning of central foveal thickness, loss of ellipsoid zone in the parafovea, and relative central foveal sparing resemble chloroquine toxicity.” 2. Quinine- or cytarabine/daunorubicin-induced optic neuropathy with bull’s-eye maculopathy was noted but excluded by history — “Optic neuropathy with bull’s eye maculopathy has been reported as an adverse effect of some drugs such as quinine and chemotherapy with a combination of cytarabine and daunorubicin.”

leakage.reason: Names niclosamide (gold word) as the timing anchor of the symptoms; the patient knows what she swallowed. The cause of the eye disease is not stated.
The accidental niclosamide ingestion is the patient's own exposure history and the key clue; the gold drug name cannot be removed without losing the history.
The fundus examination reports 'bull's-eye maculopathy' (a gold word); it is the observed appearance, not the cause.

notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation with 3 years of bilateral vision loss and photopsia (s001–s006), with the eye examination and testing at that visit (s007–s012).

The earlier treatment with oral corticosteroids for presumed optic neuritis (s003) is past history before the index visit, so it is a patient fact (diagnosis she was given, the medicine, and its effect).
